Chapter 8: Staying Awake—Maintaining Growth in Everyday Life
You know, it’s so easy to slide back into old habits once life picks up speed again. Maybe you’ve noticed it yourself—the lessons you learned during quieter times can fade quickly as new routines, relationships, and responsibilities take over. But here’s the thing: real growth doesn’t stop just because the waiting is over. It’s a daily choice—an ongoing practice to stay awake to your own needs, your feelings, and those familiar patterns that keep showing up.
Picture this—a man who had finally found some peace in solitude. Life felt good, and he was feeling strong. But when his new relationship hit a rough patch, he started feeling restless. That old urge to just run away, to distract himself, crept back in.
But this time, he did something different. He paused. He remembered what he’d learned before—the value of sitting with discomfort, of really listening to his own heart. Instead of running, he stayed. He talked things through, even though it was tough. And something amazing happened. The relationship deepened, and so did his sense of self.
Most of us don’t notice how quickly we can slip back into autopilot. The truth is, growth isn’t a destination—it’s a process. It’s about checking in with yourself, noticing when those old habits start to creep in, and choosing a new path. Even when life gets busy, it’s about making a little space for reflection.
Let’s look at another example: a woman who’d learned how to set healthy boundaries. But at work, she caught herself falling right back into those people-pleasing habits. She was feeling resentful, exhausted.
Instead of blaming her boss or her coworkers, she stopped and asked herself, “What do I need right now? How can I take care of myself?” The answer was simple—she needed to say no, to ask for help, to rest. The meantime had taught her something powerful: self-care isn’t selfish. It’s essential.
So, what does it really mean to maintain growth? It means staying connected to the practices that nourish you—maybe that’s journaling, meditation, spending time in nature, or having honest conversations. It’s reaching out for support when you need it, and offering support to others when you can. The meantime becomes your touchstone—a reminder of what’s possible when you choose to live with intention.
As the days unfold, those lessons from the meantime start to weave themselves into the fabric of your everyday life. You’ll notice a new sense of resilience, a deeper trust in yourself, and this quiet confidence that, whatever comes your way, you’ve got the tools to handle it.
The meantime, once a place of uncertainty, becomes your source of strength. And that’s something you can carry with you—every single day.
